skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: T2 gave a full warning at the start: counsel represents the Committee and company only, not the witness, and cannot give legal advice.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explained the privilege belongs to the company, which may waive it and disclose what is learned without the witness's consent.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 explained how the interview would proceed, asked for complete answers, said to flag speculation, and asked the witness to separate memory from reconstruction.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asked if the witness understood; T4 asked them to restate who was represented and who controls privilege, and T5 confirmed it correctly.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T312 ended with 'That's all I have time for today' with no check for anything else, no confidentiality or record-retention reminder, and no next steps.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Generally moved from role and background to specific transactions and then documents, though the order jumped between topics at times.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions were single and clear, such as T56 and T142, with a few compound prompts such as T150.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Stayed polite and neutral, using 'Help me understand' phrasing even when the witness bristled at T262 and T306.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: Followed the Foundation and Southampton answers into documents and figures, and pressed the Raptor return claims, but stayed close to the outline elsewhere.

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Many evasions are challenged, but T271 'I don't believe it came up' and T311 were left unchallenged, and T308 accepted a reframing of T307.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Covered who, what, when and how for LJM1, the Rhythms unwind, Chewco, the Southampton investment and the buyout, though the 2.6M payment was left thin.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: Used the November 1997 minutes, the Southampton agreement, the LJM2 report and the Kopper note to refresh recollection.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: Separated first-hand from secondhand knowledge, e.g. T56-57 on Skilling telling the Board and T226-227 on the Committee's view.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.

skills.name: Other Evidence
